title: 'He's Not Pervy': Jennifer Lawrence Reveals Why She Didn't Need Intimacy Coordinator With Robert Pattinson | Hollywood News - News18
text: Jennifer Lawrence says trust, not choreography, defined her intimate scenes with Robert Pattinson in her new film Die My Love. The Oscar-winning actor revealed that she didn’t work with an intimacy coordinator while shooting the film – not because she dismissed the idea, but because she felt “completely safe" with her co-star. During a chat on the Las Culturistas podcast, Lawrence said her comfort level with Pattinson made the experience easy and natural. “We did not have [an intimacy coordinator] — or maybe we did, but we didn’t really. I felt really safe with Rob," she said, adding that the process never felt awkward or uncomfortable. Calling Pattinson “professional and grounded," Lawrence credited his off-screen stability for the respectful atmosphere on set. “He is not pervy and very in love with [his partner] Suki Waterhouse. We mostly talked about our kids and relationships. There was never any weird, like, ‘Does he think I like him?’ If there was even a bit of that, I’d probably have an intimacy coordinator. But he was not like that." The No Hard Feelings star shot the film while pregnant with her second child, a phase she says changed how she viewed her body. “I don’t care about nudity. I’m not sensitive about it," she shared. “Being pregnant took away a lot of vanity anxiety. Before No Hard Feelings, I was dieting and not eating carbs, working out all the time. But for Die My Love, I was like – what was I gonna do, not eat? I was working 15 hours a day and just tired. They once sent me a close-up of cellulite asking if I wanted it touched up, and I said, ‘No. That’s an ass.’" Directed by Lynne Ramsay, Die My Love explores a woman’s mental unraveling after childbirth, with Pattinson playing her husband. Lawrence said she wanted Ramsay to have “total artistic freedom," trusting the filmmaker completely. Early screenings have drawn rave reviews, with critics praising Lawrence’s raw performance. The film releases on 7 November via Mubi and is already being tipped for awards buzz.
